image_description: A close-up, low-angle shot of a hammerhead shark swimming in dark blue water. The shark is viewed from below and the side, highlighting its white ventral surface and the underside of its cephalofoil. The distinctive T-shaped head is prominent, with one eye clearly visible at the tip. Other sharks are visible in the blurred background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic T-shaped cephalofoil extending laterally from the body axis.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible eye is located precisely at the distal end of the left wing of the cephalofoil.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostrils are located on the ventral side of the cephalofoil. Due to the angle of the shot and the resolution, they are not distinctly visible or verifiable against the skin texture.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior (front) edge of the cephalofoil is facing away from the camera or obscured by perspective; we primarily see the ventral and posterior aspects.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the torso shows a smooth, tapered profile consistent with a streamlined aquatic body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside (ventral) is stark white/light grey, transitioning to darker tones on the upper edges, matching the counter-shading description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: At this resolution and lighting, individual dermal denticles are not resolvable. The skin appears smooth, which is typical for macro photography of wet surfaces unless highly magnified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The first dorsal fin is on the top (dorsal) side of the shark and is completely occluded by the body in this ventral-side view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The right pectoral fin is clearly visible in the foreground, exhibiting a broad, triangular shape attached to the lower body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail (caudal fin) is outside the frame or heavily blurred in the background.

artifact_observations.location: Ventral surface of the cephalofoil and throat area
artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin texture appears overly smooth and plastic-like, lacking the subtle micro-texture expected of shark skin, even if denticles aren't individually visible. There is a slight 'waxy' sheen inconsistent with natural wetness.
The mouth area appears as a indistinct, dark smudge without clear definition of lips or jaw structure. It blends into the neck area rather than showing a distinct anatomical separation.

artifact_observations.location: Connection of pectoral fin to body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The attachment point of the visible pectoral fin seems slightly ambiguous, with soft edges that make it unclear if it is fused correctly to the body wall or floating slightly above it.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and rule out generic shark misclassification.
To verify the structural integrity of the pectoral fin attachment and ensure no fusion artifacts with the background or body.
To analyze the 'plastic' skin texture and lighting consistency, checking for generative smoothness artifacts.
To ensure the shark is properly separated from the background sharks and has valid 3D volume.

focus_areas: Skin texture realism vs. AI smoothing
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the mouth/jaw area. In many AI-generated sharks, the ventral features (mouth, gill slits) are often melted or undefined. Check if the 'smoothness' of the skin is an artifact of generation or just high-quality rendering. Verify if the eye placement is anatomically precise relative to the cephalofoil tip.
